 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The fourth round of the Portuguese Cup kicked off this Friday (20), with giants Porto taking on União Sport Clube Paredes, a club from the local third division.
 And the clash at the Estádio do Dragão featured an own goal that was hard to explain.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement You have to see it to (try to) understand what was going through Francisco Moura's mind.
 The Dragons were leading thanks to Seko Fofana's goal before the No. 74 stole the spotlight for all the wrong reasons.
 Moura asked to be substituted, and his request was granted 13 minutes after the incident.
 Regulation time ended with the score at 1–1, sending the game into extra time.
 The two 15-minute halves were not enough to produce a winner.
 And Porto prevailed 3–1 on penalties after three saves from Cláudio Ramos.
 Paredes lead Group A of Liga 3, the local third tier, by a comfortable margin.
 Porto, meanwhile, the back-to-back reigning national champions, have won all 11 of their matches in this season's Liga Portugal.
